speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To help me understand the cause, how long has this lesion been present, and does it have a history of recurring in the same area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis (visceral or localized) secondary to immunosuppression from Crohn's disease and corticosteroid use. The history of an insect bite followed by a progressive ulcerative lesion in an immunocompromised host is highly suggestive of this parasitic infection. Please proceed with a skin biopsy for histopathology and PCR confirmation.
